name: HT Media Ltd
title: HT Media Ltd - 532662 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue up 5% to INR 502 cr and EBITDA up 26% to INR 88 cr, but print margins squeezed by newsprint and circulation flat; radio and digital shrinking as stations surrendered.

triggers.label: Ad revenue up on volume and DAVP pricing

summary.headline: HT Media consolidated revenue rose 5% YoY to INR 502 cr and EBITDA 26% to INR 88 cr, with margin at 17% vs 15%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 5% YoY to INR 502 cr and EBITDA rose 26% to INR 88 cr, lifting EBITDA margin to 17% from 15%, despite the festive season shifting about 20 days into Q3. PAT came in at INR 39 cr, with PAT margin up from 4% to 8%, and net cash stood at INR 930 cr. Print drove the quarter on advertising growth, while Radio and Digital revenues fell sharply after station rationalisation and portfolio pruning. Management flagged newsprint cost and rupee depreciation as continuing margin pressures.

financial_highlights.change: PAT margin 8% vs 4% a year ago
~9% margin; first positive after many quarters

segments.name: Print
segments.commentary: Operating revenue INR 386 cr (+8%): English +5%, Hindi +11%, driven by advertising volume gains and DAVP-linked government pricing. Operating EBITDA nearly flat (-6%) on newsprint costs and festive revenue shifting to Q3.

segments.name: Radio
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 25 cr (-23%) after surrendering loss-making stations. Operating EBITDA turned positive at INR 2 cr (~9% margin); PBT improved to negative INR 2 cr from negative INR 8 cr.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 28 cr (-30%) on a leaner portfolio; operating EBITDA about INR 1 cr, breakeven to slightly positive. Management cited modest sequential improvement in revenue and profitability.

segments.name: Unallocated
segments.commentary: Corporate costs, KMP remuneration, auditor fees and mark-to-market movements; INR 12.37 cr loss, described as consistent across quarters apart from MTM variations.

guidance_outlook: Management gave no forward-looking estimates; cautionary statement issued at start of call.
Newsprint costs have flattened at a high level; management believes they have peaked but gave no timeline for easing, citing rupee, freight and currency uncertainty.

Radio profitability expected to improve substantially only after government revises the license fee structure (GOPA framework); no timing given. Management said Radio will remain profitable and stop consuming cash, but will not make a large jump from here.
Festive season shift of about 20 days will be reflected in Q3 FY27 results.
capex_capacity: Radio: rationalised station network by surrendering loss-making stations and frequencies to the government, leaving a smaller network.
HMVL board outcome listed new AFE (Ad for Equity) investments of INR 25 cr, INR 13.51 cr and INR 50 cr, per analyst question.
Management stated there are no further capital allocation decisions under way at present; any future decisions would be brought to the earnings forum.
Copies held flat; management said it will not boost copies without need and will run schemes only where required.
demand_pricing: Print ad growth attributed to market share consolidation in Hindi and English, plus the industry DAVP price increase from last year, mainly government revenue.
Management said the copy base is in a comfortable position versus competition market by market; circulation flat with no volume push.
Variable (direct) costs rose significantly YoY because of higher rates, which management described as price-led growth.
Employee costs at consolidated level about INR 95 cr vs INR 99 cr QoQ and INR 105 cr YoY, attributed to indirect cost rationalisation.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 5% and 10% ad revenue growth in English and Hindi, and does it hold for both?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited volume and market share consolidation in both languages plus DAVP-led government pricing; Diwali shift to Q3 was a drag. Confirmed as applying to both English and Hindi.

qa_highlights.question: Why is circulation revenue not disclosed and are copies being boosted?
qa_highlights.answer: Circulation revenue was flat at INR 54 cr consolidated and INR 39 cr at HMVL. Copies held flat; no push beyond need-based schemes, given high newsprint costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any respite expected in newsprint costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices have flattened at a high level with no downward move yet; management believes they have topped out, but timing depends on currency, freight and other factors.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee expenses fall at consolidated level but rise at HMVL?
qa_highlights.answer: Group-wide indirect cost rationalisation including people. HMVL variations stem from one-off reversals or timing differences; H1 HMVL costs flat to lower.

qa_highlights.question: What are HMVL's new AFE investments of INR 25 cr, INR 13.51 cr and INR 50 cr?
qa_highlights.answer: These are Ad for Equity investments, which bring future advertisers and investment positions into the company.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Radio outlook and will the unallocated loss persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Radio needs a government license fee revision for a big profit jump; no further slip into losses expected. Unallocated costs (corporate costs, KMP pay, MTM on investments) are consistent across quarters and will continue to show as a loss.

qa_highlights.question: Is management engaging with the significant shareholder Mr. Matthew Cyriac, and is capital allocation changing after OTTplay stopped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed ongoing conversations with the substantial shareholder but declined to detail them. No capital allocation decisions are under way; any would be brought to the forum when they arise.

risks_watch: Newsprint and rupee-driven cost pressure on Print margins; management says it has peaked but gave no easing timeline.
Radio profitability depends on government license fee reform, which has not yet come.
Festive shift to Q3 means Q2 vs Q3 comparisons will be distorted; watch Q3 print ad growth.
Unallocated corporate costs of INR 12.37 cr with MTM swings on investments; Digital revenue down 30% YoY.
Shareholder engagement with a substantial shareholder and open capital allocation questions; no guidance given.
Circulation disclosure format changed this quarter (new template with no absolute ad revenue numbers), limiting comparability.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the headline numbers and Print momentum, but guarded on forward view: repeatedly declined to give guidance, and gave evasive answers on the significant shareholder and capital allocation. Frank that margins face newsprint and currency pressure.
key_quotes: As we enter the festive quarter, the Company remains focused on strengthening its core businesses and maintaining financial discipline.
So, once the second step happens, the profitability will definitely return in a big way to the entire terrestrial FM radio business.
Our Board is running the affairs of the Company.

growth.why: No forward estimates given; management said Q2 print growth came from share gains and DAVP pricing, Radio is rationalised with station surrenders, and Digital revenue fell 30%, with no specific capacity or orders behind any outlook.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 17% from 15% on Print pricing and indirect cost cuts (employee cost INR 95 cr vs INR 105 cr YoY), but management flagged newsprint and rupee pressure with no easing timeline and Radio gains depend on a government fee revision.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Radio is shrinking through station surrenders, copies are held flat with no circulation push, and no new plant, line or branch was announced.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Print ad growth of +8% (English +5%, Hindi +11%) came from share gains and DAVP pricing, but copies are flat and Digital revenue fell 30% YoY, so volume growth is not guided.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said no further capital allocation decisions are under way, and copies and capacity are being held flat, so utilisation is not pushing a new capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no forward-looking estimates and issued only a cautionary statement at the start of the call.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Festive shift of about 20 days into Q3 distorts comparisons, and newsprint and rupee costs remain high with no easing timeline.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launch was discussed on the call.

rows.label: Radio license fee (GOPA) revision
rows.why: Management said Radio profitability improves substantially only after the government revises the license fee structure, with no timing given; Radio PBT is still negative INR 2 cr.

rows.label: Substantial shareholder engagement
rows.why: Management confirmed ongoing talks with the substantial shareholder Mr. Matthew Cyriac but declined to give details, so capital allocation changes remain open.

rows.label: Indirect cost rationalisation
rows.why: Consolidated employee costs fell to about INR 95 cr from INR 105 cr YoY and INR 99 cr QoQ, and management attributes this to indirect cost rationalisation.

tone.note: Management was confident on Print share gains, DAVP pricing and the 26% EBITDA rise, but cautious on newsprint and rupee costs and gave no guidance; analysts pressed on the substantial shareholder and capital allocation, which management answered evasively.
